title: Rejection for Different Inputs
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let $n,s,C\in\mathbb N$ with $C\ge |Q|+6k+5$, where $Q$ is its state set. If $x$ and $y$ are distinct Boolean inputs, each of length $n$, then for any configurations $c$ on $x$ and $d$ on $y$, the adjacency formula evaluated on the concatenation of their configuration encodings is false.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols
n, s, and C are natural numbers
C is at least the number of states of M plus 6k+5
x and y are Boolean inputs of length n
c is a configuration on x
d is a configuration on y
